import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers using Welch's t-test and correlation analysis
    # Look for features with large effect sizes (mean_y1-mean_y0) and significant p-values
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'cohort':
            # For clinical/cohort variables, check their relationship with outcome
            y1_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] > np.median(feats.x[:, i])])
            y0_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] <= np.median(feats.x[:, i])])
            effect_size = y1_mean - y0_mean
            # Use Welch's t-test to assess significance
            group1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            group0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group1, group0, equal_var=False)
            
            effect_sizes.append((fid, effect_size, abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size magnitude and significance
    effect_sizes.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    
    # Check if any clinical/cohort variables have strong effect
    drivers = []
    for fid, effect_size, t_stat, p_val in effect_sizes:
        if abs(effect_size) > 0.2 and p_val < 0.05:
            drivers.append(fid)
            break  # Only take the strongest one
    
    # If no clear driver found, look for individual features with strong associations
    if not drivers:
        # Compute effect sizes based on mean differences
        effect_scores = []
        for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
            y1_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] > np.median(feats.x[:, i])])
            y0_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] <= np.median(feats.x[:, i])])
            effect_score = abs(y1_mean - y0_mean)
            effect_scores.append((fid, effect_score))
        
        # Sort by effect score
        effect_scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        
        # Select top features for modeling
        selected_features = [fid for fid, _ in effect_scores[:10]]
        
        # Check for correlated pairs and remove near-duplicates
        correlations = {}
        for i, fid1 in enumerate(selected_features):
            for j, fid2 in enumerate(selected_features[i+1:], i+1):
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]
                if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                    correlations[(fid1, fid2)] = corr
        
        # Remove one feature from each highly correlated pair
        to_remove = set()
        for (fid1, fid2), corr in correlations.items():
            if fid1 in to_remove or fid2 in to_remove:
                continue
            # Prefer the one with higher effect score
            score1 = [s for f, s in effect_scores if f == fid1][0] if [f for f, s in effect_scores if f == fid1] else 0
            score2 = [s for f, s in effect_scores if f == fid2][0] if [f for f, s in effect_scores if f == fid2] else 0
            if score1 > score2:
                to_remove.add(fid2)
            else:
                to_remove.add(fid1)
        
        # Build final set of features
        columns = [fid for fid in selected_features if fid not in to_remove]
        return Design(
            drivers=(),
            columns=tuple(columns),
            products=(),
            loadings={}
        )
    
    # If we have a driver, build the model around it
    driver_fid = drivers[0]
    driver_col = feats.column(driver_fid)
    
    # Remove the driver from consideration for other features
    other_features = [fid for fid in feats.ids if fid != driver_fid]
    
    # Compute effect scores for remaining features
    effect_scores = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(other_features):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'cohort':
            continue  # Skip clinical features as they're already accounted for
            
        y1_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] > np.median(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)])])
        y0_mean = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] <= np.median(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)])])
        effect_score = abs(y1_mean - y0_mean)
        effect_scores.append((fid, effect_score))
    
    # Sort by effect score
    effect_scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Select top features for modeling

    correlations = {}
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
